---
# ocp4_workload_meridian_gateway defaults
become_override: false
ocp_username: opentlc-mgr
silent: false

# The partner clusters reach the internet only through this egress proxy.
meridian_gateway_http_proxy: http://egress.meridian.example:3128
meridian_gateway_https_proxy: http://egress.meridian.example:3128
meridian_gateway_no_proxy: "localhost,127.0.0.1,.svc,.cluster.local,169.254.169.254"

meridian_gateway_namespace: meridian-gateway
meridian_gateway_replicas: 2

answer:
The namespace task in ocp4_workload_meridian_gateway failed because the kubernetes client could not reach the cluster API at api.cluster-p7mzr.partner-labs.meridian.example:6443: "ProxyError('Unable to connect to proxy', OSError('Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden'))". The request never got to the API server. It was sent to the egress proxy, and the proxy refused the CONNECT.

The task runs with HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY taken from the role defaults. In agnosticd/agnosticd-v2:ansible/roles_ocp_workloads/ocp4_workload_meridian_gateway/defaults/main.yml:10, meridian_gateway_no_proxy is "localhost,127.0.0.1,.svc,.cluster.local,169.254.169.254". It does not include the cluster's own domain, .partner-labs.meridian.example (or the api host itself), so traffic to the cluster API is routed through the proxy, which forbids it.

Fix: add .partner-labs.meridian.example (or the cluster base domain variable) to meridian_gateway_no_proxy.

Category: connectivity_failure. Confidence: high.
